summary: This informational document gives guidelines for people serving as an IETF liaison to another organization, such as a standards body or industry forum. It expands on the roles of liaison managers and representatives, including their mandate, expectations, tasks and responsibilities. The IAB procedures for liaisons are in RFC 4052.

eli5.summary: When the IETF works with another group, someone acts as messenger. This is the job description for that messenger.

questions: how does the ietf work with other standards bodies
subtitle: Guidelines for people who speak on behalf of the IETF to other standards organizations.

tldr.problem: The IETF frequently needs to communicate and coordinate with other standards bodies and consortia. This coordination requires appointed people to speak for the IETF and relay information.
tldr.mechanism: The IAB appoints liaison managers and representatives to serve as two-way communication channels with peer organizations, understanding both IETF consensus and the concerns of the other organization.
tldr.outcome: Clear guidelines enable liaisons to represent the IETF accurately, avoid conflicts of interest, and build personal relationships that reduce coordination problems between organizations.

facts.label: Liaison types
facts.value: Liaison manager (primary contact) and liaison representative (focuses on specific aspects)

facts.label: Mandate scope
facts.value: Strictly limited to conveying IETF consensus

facts.label: Liaison decision
facts.value: Only initiated by IETF chair, IAB chair, Area Directors, or working group chairs

today: RFC 4691 is an Informational document and provides ongoing guidance for IETF liaison managers and representatives. The procedures and expectations it describes remain the standard for IETF liaisons with other organizations.

sections.title: Why the IETF Needs Liaisons
sections.content:
The IETF develops Internet standards but must coordinate with many other organizations: Standards Development Organizations like ITU-T and IEEE, consortia like W3C, and industry forums like the Global Grid Forum. These groups develop related standards, so the IETF and its partners need to avoid conflicting specifications and share important information.

A liaison manager is appointed by the IAB to act as the official channel of communication between the IETF and another organization. Sometimes a liaison representative handles a specific aspect of the relationship. The liaison serves both sides: reporting the other organization's plans and concerns back to the IETF, and communicating the IETF's position to the other organization.
sections.eli5: The IETF works with other groups on related problems. A liaison is the official messenger who keeps both sides informed about what the other is doing.

sections.title: What Liaisons Can and Cannot Do
sections.content:
The liaison's mandate is strictly limited: they convey IETF consensus to the other organization. A liaison MUST NOT send statements to the other organization on their own initiative. Liaison statements are only sent when initiated by the IETF chair, the IAB chair, Area Directors, or working group chairs, following the formal process in RFC 4052.

Because the IETF operates on rough consensus, the right to speak for the IETF cannot be delegated entirely. The liaison must ensure they understand the actual IETF consensus before speaking on its behalf, not just their own opinion. The liaison is an IETF representative, not an independent voice.
sections.eli5: The liaison speaks for the IETF, but only after checking what the IETF actually agrees on. They cannot just send messages whenever they want; someone in charge has to ask them to.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities and Tasks
sections.content:
The liaison manager has several critical responsibilities:

  • Attend meetings and participate in discussions with the other organization to learn what they are planning and understand their concerns
  • Report this information back to the IETF in a timely way, either in writing or verbally, so the IETF can make informed decisions
  • Ensure the other organization understands the IETF's consensus position, especially when the two organizations disagree
  • Oversee incoming liaison statements and make sure they reach the right IETF group, and that responses are prepared promptly
  • Prepare written updates about the other organization's activities as requested by the IAB or Area Directors
  • Help prepare outgoing IETF liaison statements based on actual IETF consensus

The liaison also works to build and maintain a personal contact network within the other organization, which is central to the role's effectiveness. Face-to-face interactions are seen as critical.
sections.eli5: The liaison pays attention to what the other group is doing, tells the IETF about it, makes sure the other group understands the IETF's answer, and helps fix misunderstandings when they happen.

sections.title: What It Takes to Do the Job Well
sections.content:
Good liaisons need several competencies:

  • Technical understanding: knowledge of the key issues in the liaison area and an understanding of both organizations' concerns
  • Process knowledge: understanding of the IETF's consensus process and the processes used by the peer organization
  • Communication skills: ability to communicate effectively with members of the peer organization, especially face-to-face
  • Perspective: commitment to promoting the IETF's interests within the scope of the liaison relationship, not the peer organization's interests within the IETF
  • Distance from the outcome: avoiding conflicts of interest; if the liaison is closely involved in the work being coordinated, deeply embedded in the peer organization's management, or financially invested in the outcome, they cannot maintain objectivity
  • Time commitment: sufficient time to allocate to the liaison relationship
  • Timeliness: promptly making the IETF aware of new developments
sections.eli5: A good liaison knows both sides' work well, listens well, can explain things clearly, stays impartial, and makes time for the job.

sections.title: Managing the Ongoing Relationship
sections.content:
The liaison manager participates in several key activities. When liaison statements are being sent out, the liaison offers their expertise on how the message will land with the peer organization. When incoming statements arrive with requests for response, the IETF commits to responding promptly and thoughtfully, based on technical merit rather than just accepting the incoming request.

Sometimes incoming statements are ambiguous or sent to the wrong IETF group or working group. In these cases, the liaison helps find the right recipient within the IETF.

The liaison also coordinates with other IETF liaison managers when the activities of two or more peer organizations overlap, and works to understand the perspective of liaison managers appointed by the peer organizations.
sections.eli5: The liaison helps make sure messages are clear, responses are thoughtful, and when there is confusion, the right people on both sides talk to each other.
